ios.desc:
ALL FUNCTIONS AND BENEFITS OF THE APP AT A GLANCE

Timetable information and route planner in one place
The app chooses the best public transport route based on real-time traffic conditions
The start page displays all connections of regional traffic, the S-Bahn, U-Bahn and tram as well as bus and ferry routes throughout Berlin and Brandenburg.
Never be at the stop too early or too late or on the wrong platform again: Real-time departure times at stops with customisable views
You can add connections/routes to your calendar or share with friends via SMS, e-mail, Twitter, WhatsApp or other messenger providers

Favourite destinations
With just one click, you can switch between your favourite destinations with no need to re-enter them each time

Ticket purchase
Whatever ticket you need, you can purchase it immediately and easily in the app:
short haul
single fare tickets
4-trip tickets
24-hour tickets (for 1 person and for small groups)
bicycle tickets for all of Berlin and Brandenburg 
tourist tickets (WelcomeCard, CityTourCard, Brandenburg-Berlin-Ticket)  
so-called “VBB-Umweltkarte” for Berlin zones AB
 Ticket usage and payment
The ticket can be used immediately after purchase
Payment by PayPal, direct debit, credit card 
Payment by prepaid
Use your VBB account in the “Handyticket Deutschland” app to buy tickets in other regions across Germany

Accessibility
Travel with no barriers: Timetable information and route calculations now come with special search options for blind and visually impaired passengers
The app is optimised for use with voice-over support
Easier travel for passengers with wheelchairs, strollers, bicycles or luggage:  The app shows the best place to board the train with barrier-free access

Keeping track
Your current journeys on all means of transport are animated and displayed LIVE in real time on a map – zoom into your surroundings and directly to your current location
All route networks in the network area (Berlin and Brandenburg) are stored in the app
In addition, all route networks are always up to date and can be used permanently offline after a single download

Ease of use
Easy to use thanks to access rights that are granted exclusively for this app. 
Contacts: Addresses from your contacts can be used in the start/destination search (e.g. search for a connection to your best friend Petra by typing in “Petra”)  
Calendar: Connections that you have already searched for and found can be added to your calendar as an appointment reminder

quotes.text:
I'm an American that's lived in Berlin for the last 7 years, and run a startup here.  This post is mostly correct; in fact, it's pretty impressive that the author soaked up the vibe that much in such a short span.  But there are a couple points worth clarifying:

The jaywalking analogy is stretched.  Like, the source of it is partly true, but it's a pretty boring social convention.  There are enough places where Berliners proudly flaunt the law that make Californians seem like straight-laced prudes.

However, what the argument gets right is that the issue is more cultural than structural.  There are a lot of things that come together to make German startup-culture somewhat tamer than the US variety, among them less of a drive for polarized go-big-or-go-home attitude, the historical strength of the German Mittelstand (medium sized companies) and less tolerance for risk.

Also, the thing on data and Google Maps seems off.  I'm not sure why Google Maps has only recently started to integrate Berlin's subway data, but there are excellent apps for Android [1] and iOS [2] that accomplish the same (and are not published by the local transit authority, and I can't imagine that solo app authors have more clout to get at the data than Google).  It seemed a bit lame to assume that since Google Maps doesn't have the data that it must be the city's fault.

[1] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.schildbach.oeffi&hl=de

[2] …
quotes.story_title: Germans and Jaywalking: An American's Perspective on the Berlin Tech Scene
